The Boston Celtics dominated the Philadelphia 76ers, 123-101, on November 10, picking up a convincing road victory in Philadelphia. Boston controlled the game offensively, putting up 123 points and pulling away from the Sixers. The win continued the Celtics’ strong start to the season, while Philadelphia was left looking for answers after struggling to keep pace with Boston on its home floor. The biggest storyline is the gap between these two Eastern Conference contenders: Boston continues to look like a legitimate championship threat, while the 76ers need more consistency if they want to compete with the conference’s best. The biggest storyline was the reunion between Jayson Tatum and Jaylen Brown. The former Celtics teammates faced each other for the first time as opponents after Boston traded Brown to Philadelphia over the summer. There was some awkwardness before tipoff, with Tatum attempting to greet Brown, who largely ignored him. Tatum finished with 21 points, six rebounds and four assists, while Brown struggled with foul trouble and managed just 13 points. Paul George, who went to Boston in the Brown trade, stole the show with 36 points in his return to Philadelphia. Tyrese Maxey led the Sixers with 24. Boston put the game away with a 14-0 run to open the fourth quarter, extending its winning streak to four games. The takeaway: Boston won the first chapter of the Tatum-Brown rivalry, and Paul George made sure his former team regretted letting him go.
